investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm) and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~139–144 s), preventing VM assignment and leaving all required eval evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, so even if vm capacity were freed those 4 nodes would still be ineligible. The 4-node affinity rejection is consistent across all three sibling failures (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: all three checks ran sequentially within ~7 minutes and each independently hit the same capacity wall, suggesting the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster is too small to absorb even a single new eval pod when existing workloads are present.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-05T14:12–14:17Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check terminated without writing any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node is eligible for scheduling. The eval pod was stuck Unschedulable for ~139–144 seconds across all three checks before the runner surfaced the failure. Because the pod never started, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent) could not create a remote agent, and zero evidence was collected, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes — the remote agent pod requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes carry, so even if quota were available on other nodes they could not be used.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or other workload may have consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and not yet released them before this eval window started, leaving zero capacity at the time all three checks ran.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-05 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a Kubernetes cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent eval pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable VM slots remaining), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both subsets. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing createAgent from completing and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty. The same scheduler error appeared independently across all three remote-agent checks within a ~5-minute window, confirming the constraint is at the cluster/node-pool level rather than in the eval runner logic itself.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm) and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~139–144 s), preventing VM assignment and leaving all required eval evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, so even if vm capacity were freed those 4 nodes would still be ineligible. The 4-node affinity rejection is consistent across all three sibling failures (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: all three checks ran sequentially within ~7 minutes and each independently hit the same capacity wall, suggesting the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster is too small to absorb even a single new eval pod when existing workloads are present.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-05 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a Kubernetes cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent eval pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable VM slots remaining), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both subsets. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing createAgent from completing and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty. The same scheduler error appeared independently across all three remote-agent checks within a ~5-minute window, confirming the constraint is at the cluster/node-pool level rather than in the eval runner logic itself.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the agent creation step is the first blocking operation and is where scheduling occurs

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=145440 is well within the outage threshold, so the failure is a hard scheduler rejection, not a latency breach
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This directly matches the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message on both capable nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the total cluster size.

TERTIARY — Concurrent eval runs or other workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are scheduled at the same time, they may transiently exhaust the small pool of 2 kata-capable nodes.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node pool scaling not triggered in time: the cluster autoscaler may not have added new kata-capable nodes before the eval timeout, or autoscaling may not be configured for this node type.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run only the remote-agent-runtime eval against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduler failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the Allocatable and Capacity fields for kata.peerpods.io/vm on each node to confirm whether slots are exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: List pending or running pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, ns: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
reproductionSteps.details: Identify which workloads are holding the limited VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect the node affinity and selector rules on the failing eval pod spec
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the pod spec for a remote-agent eval pod (or the createAgent template) to verify whether the affinity/selector rules correctly target the kata-capable nodes and whether those rules are current.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduler constraint
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the constraint is confirmed at the cluster level.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents eval checks — production-api (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with identical Kubernetes scheduler errors; the feature is registered at infra/evals/status/features.json lines 176–189.
affectedAreas.details: remote-agent-create (required=true) and remote-agent-state (required=true) are required checks; their failure contributes to feature degraded/outage thresholds (degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2).

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool — production cluster
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod workloads, indicating the extended resource is fully consumed.
affectedAreas.details: Only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource; the other 4 are excluded by node affinity/selector, making the effective schedulable pool very small.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent eval runner — createAgent call
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) as the first blocking step; the pod scheduling failure prevents this call from completing, leaving all evidence fields empty.
affectedAreas.details: Source context at lines 1913–1918 of run-status-probes.mjs shows the eval entry point and the createAgent invocation.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message, plus an assertion that message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura'. None of these were satisfied because the agent never started.
affectedAreas.details: All 5 required evidence fields are listed in expected-output.missing-required-evidence.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes using kubectl describe nodes; if slots are at zero, identify and terminate any idle or leaked eval pods holding those slots.

Review whether the node affinity/selector rules on the remote agent pod template are intentionally restricting scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and whether those rules can be relaxed or whether additional kata-capable nodes should be added to the pool.

Investigate whether concurrent eval runs or production remote-agent workloads are competing for the same limited VM slots; consider serializing eval runs or adding a pre-flight capacity check before launching remote-agent evals.
Assess whether the kata-capable node pool should be scaled up (more nodes or more VM slots per node) to accommodate both production workloads and eval probes running simultaneously.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are registered as required=true checks (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 183–184) and the feature has degradedAfterFailures=1, confirm the current feature health status and whether any alerting thresholds have been crossed.

Review Kubernetes cluster autoscaler configuration for the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool to determine whether scale-out is possible and whether the eval timeout (outageLatencyMs=420000) is long enough to accommodate autoscaler warm-up time.

recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Look for Capacity vs. Allocatable values; if Allocatable is 0 on both kata-capable nodes, capacity exhaustion is confirmed.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies which workloads are holding the limited VM slots, distinguishing between eval contention and production workload saturation.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: If eval pods from prior runs are stuck in Terminating state, they may be holding slots that should have been released.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduler constraint is still present or was transient; a pass would indicate the cluster recovered.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Retrieve the node affinity and selector rules from the remote agent pod template
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies whether the 4 non-kata nodes are correctly excluded or whether the selector is overly restrictive, shrinking the schedulable pool unnecessarily.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Compare the pod's nodeSelector and affinity.nodeAffinity rules against the actual node labels on all 6 nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Surfaces the exact scheduler event with timestamp, pod name, and node rejection reasons, corroborating the message in failed-check.message.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Cross-reference the event timestamp with the eval endedAt=2026-07-05T14:17:03.998Z.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (non-zero allocatable slots) at the time of the eval run, the 'Insufficient' message would need another explanation such as a quota or admission webhook.

If the eval pod spec carried incorrect resource requests (e.g., requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm when it should not), the scheduler message would be a misconfiguration rather than true capacity exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector rules were found to be intentionally excluding the 4 non-kata nodes for a valid reason, the root cause would shift entirely to the 2-node capacity ceiling rather than a selector misconfiguration.

If no other pods were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of failure, it would suggest the nodes themselves were unhealthy or the resource was not properly advertised, not that capacity was consumed by competing workloads.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a scheduling timeout failure.
Add a dedicated eval for remote-agent node pool health that asserts at least N kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and that the expected number of nodes match the pod's affinity/selector rules.

Introduce a sibling check correlation eval that detects when all checks under a feature fail with the same scheduler error pattern and automatically escalates to a cluster-level capacity alert rather than treating each check as an independent failure.
Add a historical baseline eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization over time so that capacity trends can be detected before full exhaustion occurs.
